subject: SCIENCE
title: Sound Starts with Vibrations
objective: Relate sound to vibration and practice hearing safety.
introduction: Pluck a string and it makes a sound! What makes sound start, and how do we keep our ears safe?

vocabulary.definition: Something you hear with your ears.
The sense that lets us listen with our ears.
A fast back-and-forth movement that makes sound.

items.prompt: Which statement about sound is true?

options.text: Sound begins with vibration and travels through a medium.

items.explanation: Sound starts when something vibrates and travels through air or other matter. It cannot travel through empty space, and loudness is not the same as pitch.

items.prompt: Which example shows how sound begins?
items.explanation: Plucking makes the string shake back and forth, and that vibration makes sound. A still string or a quiet room makes no sound.

items.prompt: Which statement about sound is NOT true?
items.explanation: Sound needs matter like air to travel through — it cannot travel through empty space. Speaker cones and plucked strings vibrate to make sound.

items.prompt: What starts sound in a plucked string?
items.explanation: The string shakes back and forth quickly, and that vibration makes the sound. Color and shadow do not make sound.
Lower volume is gentler on your ears, so it protects hearing. Max volume can hurt your ears, and sound cannot travel through empty space.
